title: An Execution‑Oriented Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Simulate→Rollback Pipelines for LLM‑Assisted NetOps: a Confirmatory Study with gpt‑5‑mini
abstract: We preregistered (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1) and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to test whether a guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline reduces actionable misconfigurations relative to a generation‑only baseline on vendor‑neutral NetOps tasks. Key frozen design elements: N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks (routing/ACL/NAT), model = gpt‑5‑mini, and a shared_initial_generation policy (one generated candidate per task that was reused across both conditions). Because the single shared candidate per task was non‑actionable for every task under the deterministic simulator, both baseline and guarded conditions produced 0 actionable misconfigurations (baseline = 0/160; guarded = 0/160), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.00). Crucially, the shared_initial_generation design choice is explicitly responsible for a ceiling effect that rendered the preregistered target (≥30% relative reduction) unevaluable. We release SHA‑256‑verified artifacts (generation outputs, provider_call logs, per‑task scoring JSONs, deterministic simulator traces, analysis scripts) and provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of this confirmatory failure mode together with prescriptive, artifact‑traceable remedies (calibration, independent per‑condition generation, simulator predicate validation).

sections.introduction: Motivation and background. Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration and change proposals. Operational deployment demands reliable safeguards so that proposed configurations are safe to enact; generate→validate→repair pipelines with deterministic gating have been advanced to provide that assurance. Research question. After a fresh literature review we preregistered (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1) the confirmatory hypothesis: does a guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline (C) reduce the actionable misconfiguration rate by ≥30% relative to a generation‑only baseline (A) on a representative vendor‑neutral NetOps task set? Preregistered contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory execution with deterministic, SHA‑256‑verified artifacts; (2) a complete, artifact‑grounded report of numeric outcomes; (3) an evidence‑based diagnosis of a ceiling‑effect failure mode created by the preregistered shared_initial_generation policy, with concrete remediations. Note on design choice: the preregistered shared_initial_generation policy (one candidate per task reused across both baseline and guarded conditions) intentionally removed generator variance to economize provider calls. We explicitly warn that this policy can create a ceiling effect when shared candidates are non‑actionable; the run reported here illustrates that exact failure mode.
sections.related_work: Verification and pipeline context. Network verification tools (VeriFlow; Batfish/Propane family) perform policy and reachability checks and motivate gating before enactment. Recent NetOps work on LLMs emphasizes generate→validate→repair architectures, constraint encoding, and workflow‑centred AIOps evaluation (e.g., OpsEval, MeshAgent, MNC). Surveys argue operational reliability stems from the surrounding verification machinery rather than raw model outputs. Our study differs by preregistering a paired estimand, executing deterministically, and publishing full SHA‑256‑verified artifacts so that the exact model outputs, validator decisions, and simulator adjudications can be re‑examined.
sections.methodology: Preregistration highlights (frozen before execution). Study id: c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1. Task corpus and selection: N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks deterministically sampled from public vendor‑neutral collections and deterministically augmented using preregistered seeds [42,123,999]; selection scripts and input hashes are archived. Model and adapter: gpt‑5‑mini (hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Generation policy (explicit preregistered choice): shared_initial_generation — exactly one generated candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded. Guarded pipeline (C): candidate → constraint validator → deterministic simulator enactment → rollback/repair if simulator labels actionable; Baseline (A): same single shared candidate but no validator/simulator gating. Adjudicator: deterministic simulator returns an actionable boolean that the analysis treats as the operational safety predicate. Primary estimand and analysis. Primary estimand: paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion (P_actionable_A − P_actionable_C) across tasks. Analysis: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for CI and McNemar exact two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes. Artifact hygiene and reproducibility. All raw model outputs, provider calls, canonicalized configurations, per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), deterministic simulator schema, and analysis scripts were archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Representative archived hashes (from the execution manifest): execution/raw_results.jsonl = 2445d0f8e9be9cfa34ede1bbe80b82d6f05b51bcafc7c1688d0ed8e1c73d8044; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv = fba3b0ca21c7c7c380ed1134b4fce48b0870bf72a7be0fd8610bf7e6b63a970b. The execution manifest lists all file paths and SHA‑256 hashes used to deterministically reproduce the run; use the included manifest (execution_manifest.json) plus the archived files to reproduce analysis and figures.

sections.discussion:
Interpretation and primary failure diagnosis. The run's degenerate outcome (zero actionable events in both conditions) is an artifact of the preregistered shared_initial_generation policy: when the single shared candidate per task is already non‑actionable under the deterministic simulator, the guarded pipeline has no opportunity to block or repair—hence no measurable reduction. This is a design‑sensitivity or ceiling‑effect failure mode of the confirmatory protocol (not evidence that guarded pipelines lack operational value). Artifact‑grounded evidence: the provider_call logs and call_cache entries (listed in the manifest) verify that exactly one generation occurred per task and that the same generated text was reused across conditions; the per‑task scoring JSONs show the simulator predicate returned actionable=false for every shared candidate. Prescriptive remedies (implementable from archived artifacts):
1) Calibration pass before a confirmatory lock: run a small independent calibration sample (e.g., 20 tasks) with independent per‑condition generation to estimate baseline actionability and create headroom; archived selection/augmentation scripts and seeds permit deterministic reselection of adversarial variants. 
2) Use independent per‑condition generation (one generation per task per condition) when the hypothesis concerns pipeline interventions, so the guarded pipeline can act on condition‑specific proposals. 
3) Validate simulator predicates against a human‑adjudicated sample to detect overly permissive simulator semantics. The analysis/contamination_summary.csv (hash 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5f...) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (hash b8404c6f...) record the automated pre‑execution checks and should be consulted during recalibration. Threats to validity. Construct validity: the deterministic simulator is a simplification of production risk and may under‑ or overapproximate enactment hazards. External validity: single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) and the specific generation policy limit generalisation; follow‑up runs with independent generation and multiple models are needed. Conclusion drawn from this execution. The confirmatory run is reproducible and deterministically archived but the preregistered shared_initial_generation policy produced a ceiling effect that made the primary hypothesis unevaluable; the scientific contribution is therefore an artifact‑backed diagnosis of this confirmatory design failure mode and actionable, artifact‑traceable remediation steps.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic, artifact‑verified paired confirmatory experiment comparing generation‑only and guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipelines using gpt‑5‑mini on N=160 vendor‑neutral NetOps tasks. Observed baseline actionable = 0/160 and guarded actionable = 0/160; paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.00). This degenerate outcome resulted from the preregistered shared_initial_generation design choice, which created a ceiling effect when all shared candidates were non‑actionable under the simulator. The run's principal scientific value is (a) full determinism and reproducibility—SHA‑256‑verified artifacts permit deterministic reanalysis—and (b) an artifact‑grounded identification of a common confirmatory design failure mode and prescriptive next steps (calibration, independent generation, simulator validation). We release the full execution manifest, per‑task scoring JSONs, provider_call logs, call_cache, and analysis artifacts; these permit deterministic reproduction and inform redesigned confirmatory tests that avoid the ceiling effect documented here. Future confirmatory work should (i) calibrate headroom, (ii) use independent per‑condition generation for pipeline contrasts, and (iii) validate simulator predicates with human adjudication or canary trials to strengthen external validity.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Models, orchestration, and autonomy: primary model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API). Orchestration/adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The Master Prompt bundle that guided the autonomous run is the Master Prompt v1 — Autonomous CNSM 2026 Research Run; the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development. Pre‑lock development and rehearsal artifacts were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence. After the autonomy lock, the autonomous system performed the literature search, research‑gap selection, preregistration (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1), prompt generation, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, manuscript drafting, and revision without manual human edits to technical content, numeric results, figures, captions, references, or this Disclosure Statement. Preregistration: the confirmatory paired design, task selection (N=160 with augmentation seeds [42,123,999]), shared_initial_generation policy (one candidate per task reused across conditions), model (gpt‑5‑mini), primary estimand, analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10,000, seed=1729 and McNemar exact), retry policy, and stopping rules were frozen before execution. Execution and artifacts: all raw model outputs, provider call logs, canonicalized configurations, per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), deterministic simulator schema, analysis scripts, and the execution manifest are archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Representative artifact hashes (recorded in the execution manifest): execution/raw_results.jsonl = 2445d0f8e9be9cfa34ede1bbe80b82d6f05b51bcafc7c1688d0ed8e1c73d8044; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv = fba3b0ca21c7c7c380ed1134b4fce48b0870bf72a7be0fd8610bf7e6b63a970b; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json = e321b84c41233594d2bebc0d01722cade9ab148516fcf13fd9788c94fb638e59; execution/scoring/task-000050-baseline.json = e4fa1208479e3d51adbdb7147ea951766fda52baefee705d2320da8870395d90; execution/scoring/task-000160-baseline.json = 6310438573e09696982a7edd299d12731966266bd66fb1470123f0b1549ba8ef. Provider calls and retries: planned maximum model calls = 320; actual provider model calls used = 160 due to the preregistered shared_initial_generation design. The retry policy allowed up to two transient retries for provider errors; none materially affected confirmatory outcomes. Human role limitations reiterated: the Research Director provided topic selection and pre‑lock infrastructure approval; after the autonomy lock no human manually edited technical manuscript content or numeric results. Reproducibility note: to reproduce the analysis deterministically, consult the included execution_manifest.json in the archived artifacts; it enumerates the file paths and SHA‑256 hashes (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl = 2445d0f8...); use those files and hashes to validate and reproduce the analysis without relying on external URLs.
limitations: Ceiling effect: the preregistered shared_initial_generation (one candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded) produced baseline actionable = 0/160, eliminating headroom and making the preregistered ≥30% relative‑reduction target unevaluable.
Single‑model and single‑policy scope: the experiment used only gpt‑5‑mini and the exact frozen generation/validation policy; generalization beyond this model and policy is unresolved.

Construct validity: the deterministic simulator adjudicator abstracts production risk; its predicate (actionable boolean) may not capture all real deployment failure modes—human adjudication or canary trials remain necessary for production claims.
External validity: no live device enactment or in‑production rollout was performed; results apply to the simulator‑backed confirmatory design executed here.

Design sensitivity: the shared‑candidate design reduces provider calls but can mask downstream intervention effects; independent per‑condition generation should be used when testing pipeline causal effects.
